what_its_for: Azelastine is an antihistamine used to relieve symptoms of allergies such as runny nose, sneezing, and nasal itching. The nasal spray is used for seasonal and year-round allergies. The eye drops are used to treat itchy, red eyes caused by allergies.
how_to_take: For the nasal spray: Gently blow your nose before using. Tilt your head slightly forward, insert the tip into one nostril, and spray while breathing in gently through your nose. Alternate nostrils as directed. Avoid spraying into your eyes. For eye drops: Tilt your head back, pull down your lower eyelid to form a small pocket, and place the prescribed number of drops inside. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Do not touch the dropper tip to your eye or any surface to keep it clean.
dosing: Nasal spray (adults and children 12 and older): Usually 1 to 2 sprays in each nostril twice a day. Children 6 to 11 years old: Usually 1 spray in each nostril twice a day. Eye drops (adults and children 3 and older): Usually 1 drop in each affected eye twice a day. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's exact instructions, as dosing can vary.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not use extra doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle upright and tightly capped when not in use. Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep out of reach of children. Eye drops may need to be discarded within a certain number of days after opening — check the label or ask your pharmacist.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while using azelastine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do other activities that require alertness until you know how this medication affects you. Avoid getting the nasal spray in your eyes. Do not wear contact lenses when using the eye drops. Wait at least 10 minutes before putting your contact lenses back in after using eye drops.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you experience: severe drowsiness or dizziness that interferes with your daily activities, nosebleeds that are severe or do not stop, painful or worsening eye irritation or vision changes (with eye drops), signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing, or if your allergy symptoms are not improving or are getting worse after a few days of use.
when_it_works: Azelastine works fairly quickly. The nasal spray usually begins to relieve symptoms within 15 to 30 minutes after use. The eye drops typically start working within a few minutes. You should notice improvement in your allergy symptoms within the first day or two of regular use.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before using azelastine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Children: The nasal spray is approved for children 6 years and older; the eye drops are approved for children 3 years and older. Do not use in younger children unless directed by a doctor. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to the drowsiness and dizziness side effects. Use with caution and talk to your doctor about the right dose for you.
